subject: cast problems if data added to molten data frames

messages.author: 7e54aa65e5af5819
messages.subject: cast problems if data added to molten data frames
parts:
In my script I am adding certain variables to already molten data.
After doing this cast stops working properly. This seems to be like a
bug to me.

Any suggestions for a workaround?


df <- data.frame(id1=rep(letters[1:2],2), id2=rep(LETTERS
[1:2],each=2), var1=1:4)

df.m <- melt(df)

df.m$value2 <- runif(4)

cast(df.m, id1~id2, value="value1")
id1 A B
1 a 1 3
2 b 2 4
cast(df.m, id1~id2, value="value2")
id1 A B
1 a 1 3
2 b 2 4

--
http://learnr.wordpress.com

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: cast problems if data added to molten data frames
parts:
Hi,

as far as I can see the problem appears when the data.frame contains a
variable "value" (e.g. as a result of melt()). In this case we end up
with two value variables after the following line in cast,

if (any(names(data) == value))
names(data)[names(data) == value] <- "value"
browser() # data has two value variables

and the first one is used regardless of the value= argument (only the
original order matters). I guess there should be a test for this, with
either a warning or perhaps a more unusual name used from this point
onwards in cast().

Best,

baptiste

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: cast problems if data added to molten data frames
parts:
Thanks to learnr for the bug report and to Baptiste for discovering
where the bug is. I've added a bug report to
http://github.com/hadley/reshape/issues/#issue/1. Unfortunately it's
unlikely I'll get to this for a while since reshape is currently in
maintenance mode. I have a big rewrite that's been in progress for
over a year (it gives considerable speed and memory performance
improvements), but unfortunately it's not high priority.

If there was anyone interested in learning more about how reshape
works and wanted to improve it, I could probably help them get
started. Even a set of comprehensive test cases would be very useful
(preferably written with testthat).

Hadley
